title: Get Started with forecastdom
text: main contribution Li, Liao, Quaedvlieg (2022). Tests whether benchmark’s conditional expected loss competitor, uniformly across conditioning states:
code: # Under the null (a = 1): benchmark weakly dominates sim_null <- do_sim(J = 3, n = 500, a = 1, c = 0, rho_u = 0.4) cspa_test(sim_null$Y, sim_null$X, level = 0.05, trim = 2) #>  #> ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │      Conditional Superior Predictive Ability       │ #> │          (Li, Liao, and Quaedvlieg, 2022)          │ #> ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ #> │ H0: Benchmark weakly dominates all competitors     │ #> │     conditionally, uniformly across all states     │ #> │ H1: Some competitor outperforms the benchmark      │ #> │     in certain conditioning states                 │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Test Results:                                      │ #> │  Theta: 0.1488                                     │ #> │  P-value: 0.4666                                   │ #> │  Significance level: 0.0500                        │ #> │  Decision: Not rejected                            │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Estimation Details:                                │ #> │  Observations (n): 480                             │ #> │  Competitors (J): 3                                │ #> │  Series terms (K): 4                               │ #> │  HAC lag order: 1 (pre-whitened)                   │ #> │  Selected (j,x) pairs: 1440 / 1440 (100.0%)        │ #> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ # Under the alternative (a = 1.5): a competitor outperforms in some states sim_alt <- do_sim(J = 3, n = 500, a = 1.5, c = 0, rho_u = 0.4) result <- cspa_test(sim_alt$Y, sim_alt$X, level = 0.05, trim = 2) result #>  #> ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │      Conditional Superior Predictive Ability       │ #> │          (Li, Liao, and Quaedvlieg, 2022)          │ #> ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ #> │ H0: Benchmark weakly dominates all competitors     │ #> │     conditionally, uniformly across all states     │ #> │ H1: Some competitor outperforms the benchmark      │ #> │     in certain conditioning states                 │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Test Results:                                      │ #> │  Theta: -0.2217                                    │ #> │  P-value: 0.0002                                   │ #> │  Significance level: 0.0500                        │ #> │  Decision: Rejected ***                            │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Estimation Details:                                │ #> │  Observations (n): 480                             │ #> │  Competitors (J): 3                                │ #> │  Series terms (K): 4                               │ #> │  HAC lag order: 1 (pre-whitened)                   │ #> │  Selected (j,x) pairs: 1440 / 1440 (100.0%)        │ #> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

text: Tests null hypothesis constant regression coefficients alternative general time variation:
code: X <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2) y2 <- X %*% c(0.5, -0.3) + rnorm(n) qll_hat(y2, X, L = floor(n^(1/3))) #>  #> ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │ Elliott-Muller Test for Time-Varying Coefficients  │ #> │             (Elliott and Muller, 2006)             │ #> ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ #> │ H0: Constant coefficients (beta(t) = beta)         │ #> │ H1: Time-varying coefficients                      │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Test Results:                                      │ #> │  qLL-hat statistic: -7.2358                        │ #> │  5% critical value: -10.64                         │ #> │  Decision (5%): Not rejected                       │ #> ├┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┤ #> │ Details:                                           │ #> │  Observations (T): 300                             │ #> │  Time-varying coefficients (k): 2                  │ #> │ Note: Non-standard distribution.                   │ #> │ Reject when qLL-hat < critical value.              │ #> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

what: Conditional Superior Predictive Ability (CSPA) Test — cspa_test
title: Conditional Superior Predictive Ability (CSPA) Test — cspa_test
text: Tests null hypothesis benchmark forecasting method conditional superior predictive ability competing alternatives, uniformly across conditioning states. Based Li, Liao, Quaedvlieg (2022).

code: cspa_test(Y, X, level, trim = 0, prewhiten = -1L, preselect = TRUE, R = 10000L)

title: Conditional Superior Predictive Ability (CSPA) Test — cspa_test
text: Y n x J matrix loss differentials respect benchmark. Positive values indicate benchmark outperforms competitor j period t. X n x 1 numeric vector conditioning variable. level Significance level (e.g., 0.05). trim Trim observations conditioning variable exceeds many standard deviations mean. Use 0 (default) trimming. prewhiten Order pre-whitening VAR HAC estimation. Use 0 standard Newey-West, -1 (default) AIC-based lag selection. preselect Logical; perform adaptive inequality selection? Default TRUE. R Integer; number bootstrap replications critical value computation. Default 10000.

title: Conditional Superior Predictive Ability (CSPA) Test — cspa_test
text: list class "cspa_test" containing: theta Infimum upper confidence bound. Negative values lead rejection null. pvalue P-value test. reject Logical; whether null rejected given level. level Significance level used. h_hat Estimated conditional mean functions (n x J matrix). sigma_jx Estimated standard deviations (J x n matrix). kp Critical value adaptive inequality selection. Vhat Logical matrix indicating selected (j, x) pairs. X Conditioning variable (trimming). Y Loss differentials (trimming). K Number series terms used. prewhiten_order Pre-whitening lag order actually used.

title: Conditional Superior Predictive Ability (CSPA) Test — cspa_test
text: Li, J., Liao, Z., Quaedvlieg, R. (2022). Conditional Superior Predictive Ability. Review Economic Studies, 89(2), 843-875.

what: Clark-West Test for Predictive Ability of Nested Models — cw_test
title: Clark-West Test for Predictive Ability of Nested Models — cw_test
text: Tests whether alternative (unrestricted) model superior --sample predictive ability relative benchmark (restricted) model, using MSFE-adjusted statistic Clark West (2007). Also computes --sample \(R^2_{OS}\) statistic.

title: Clark-West Test for Predictive Ability of Nested Models — cw_test
Clark-West Test for Predictive Ability of Nested Models — cw_test
text: e1 Numeric vector forecast errors benchmark (restricted/null) model. e2 Numeric vector forecast errors alternative (unrestricted) model. f1 Numeric vector forecasts benchmark model. f2 Numeric vector forecasts alternative model.

title: Clark-West Test for Predictive Ability of Nested Models — cw_test
text: list class "cw_test" containing: statistic Clark-West t-statistic. pvalue One-sided p-value (H1: alternative better). r2os --sample \(R^2_{OS}\) percent. n Number observations.

title: Clark-West Test for Predictive Ability of Nested Models — cw_test
text: MSFE-adjusted series defined : $$\hat{f}_t = e_{1,t}^2 - \left(e_{2,t}^2 - (f_{1,t} - f_{2,t})^2\right)$$ test regresses \(\hat{f}_t\) constant uses resulting t-statistic, compared standard normal distribution (one-sided).

title: Clark-West Test for Predictive Ability of Nested Models — cw_test
text: Clark, T.E. West, K.D. (2007). Approximately Normal Tests Equal Predictive Accuracy Nested Models. Journal Econometrics, 138(1), 291-311.

Clark-McCracken ENC-NEW Encompassing Test — enc_new
text: Tests whether benchmark model encompasses alternative model, using ENC-NEW statistic Clark McCracken (2001). null, benchmark forecast encompasses alternative (additional information alternative).

title: Clark-McCracken ENC-NEW Encompassing Test — enc_new
Clark-McCracken ENC-NEW Encompassing Test — enc_new
text: e1 Numeric vector forecast errors benchmark model. e2 Numeric vector forecast errors alternative model.

title: Clark-McCracken ENC-NEW Encompassing Test — enc_new
text: list class "enc_new" containing: statistic ENC-NEW test statistic. n Number observations.

title: Clark-McCracken ENC-NEW Encompassing Test — enc_new
text: ENC-NEW statistic : $$\text{ENC-NEW} = n \cdot \frac{\bar{c}}{\text{MSFE}_2}$$ \(\bar{c} = n^{-1} \sum (e_{1,t}^2 - e_{2,t} e_{1,t})\) \(\text{MSFE}_2 = n^{-1} \sum e_{2,t}^2\). Critical values non-standard depend estimation setup. See Clark McCracken (2001, Table 2) asymptotic critical values.

title: Clark-McCracken ENC-NEW Encompassing Test — enc_new
text: Clark, T.E. McCracken, M.W. (2001). Tests Equal Forecast Accuracy Encompassing Nested Models. Journal Econometrics, 105(1), 85-110.

title: Unconditional Superior Predictive Ability (USPA/SPA) Test — spa_test
